This is achieved by applying a sequence of Householder reflections H_k = I - 2(v_k v_k^T) / (v_k^T v_k) to zero out the sub-diagonal elements of each column. To avoid catastrophic cancellation, the vector v_k is chosen such that the reflection maps the column vector to a multiple of the first standard basis vector, with the sign chosen to match the sign of the first element of the column vector. def householder(A): '''Inputs: A : Matrix of size m*n, m>=n Outputs: A : Matrix of size m*n, where the upper triangle contains R ''' m, n = A.shape A = A.astype(float) for k in range(n): x = A[k:m, k] norm_x = np.linalg.norm(x) v = x.copy() v[0] += np.sign(x[0]) * norm_x if x[0] != 0 else norm_x norm_v = np.linalg.norm(v) if norm_v > 1e-15: v = v / norm_v A[k:m, k:n] -= 2 * np.outer(v, v.T @ A[k:m, k:n]) return A ```
